title: Dublin Table Quiz

questions.q: Which river flows through the centre of Dublin?
Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000-year lease on which Dublin brewery site in 1759?
Which illuminated Gospel book, Ireland's most famous medieval manuscript, is on display in Trinity College Dublin's Old Library?
Which building on O'Connell Street served as the rebels' headquarters during the 1916 Easter Rising?
What name is given to the 16 June celebration of James Joyce's novel Ulysses?
The name Dublin comes from the Irish "Dubh Linn". What does it mean in English?
Which Dublin stadium is the headquarters of the Gaelic Athletic Association?
Which large Dublin park is home to Áras an Uachtaráin and a herd of wild fallow deer?
Which Dublin-born author wrote the 1897 novel Dracula?
In the song about Molly Malone, what does she sell as she wheels her barrow?

notes: River Liffey flows through Dublin city centre; see River Liffey Wikipedia
9,000-year lease at St James's Gate signed 31 December 1759; see Guinness Storehouse history / Guinness Wikipedia
Book of Kells. Trinity also holds the Book of Durrow, hence 'most famous'.
GPO was headquarters of the Rising; see GPO Witness History / Easter Rising Wikipedia
Bloomsday, 16 June, the day Ulysses is set (1904); see Bloomsday Wikipedia / James Joyce Centre
Dubh Linn = black pool; see Dublin Wikipedia (etymology) / Dublin City Council
Croke Park is GAA headquarters; see GAA.ie / Croke Park Wikipedia
Áras an Uachtaráin and fallow deer herd in Phoenix Park; see OPW Phoenix Park site
Stoker born in Clontarf, Dublin, 1847; Dracula published 1897; see Bram Stoker Wikipedia
Lyric "crying cockles and mussels, alive, alive, oh"; see Molly Malone Wikipedia
